name: Casa do Baile (Pampulha Dance Hall)
features: Round dance hall on an island, with a free-form canopy that snakes along the lake shore.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Pampulha Modern Ensemble, Niemeyer (UNESCO 2016)
note: Part of the UNESCO Pampulha Modern Ensemble (2016) with the church and casino already on the wall. Fourth photo is mostly the entrance sign.

name: Iate Tênis Clube, Pampulha
features: Lakeside club under an inverted 'butterfly' roof, raised on pilotis, one of Niemeyer's four Pampulha buildings.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Pampulha Modern Ensemble, Niemeyer (UNESCO 2016)
note: The club has been altered over the years; photos show it from across the lake.

name: Oca, Ibirapuera Park
features: Low white concrete dome pierced by round windows, with curving ramps and floors inside.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Ibirapuera Park ensemble, Niemeyer
note: Ibirapuera Auditorium (2005) is already on the wall; the Oca and Bienal pavilion are the 1954 originals.

name: Bienal Pavilion (Pavilhão Ciccillo Matarazzo)
features: Long glass-and-louvre box on a column grid; curved ramps and free-form floor openings inside.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Ibirapuera Park ensemble, Niemeyer

photos.file: File:Fachada do prédio da Bienal de São Paulo.jpg

note: Photos seen are the entrance and a louvre close-up; no wide view of the whole building checked. Home of the São Paulo Bienal since 1957. Many interior photos in the category.

name: Grande Hotel de Ouro Preto
features: Modern hotel set into a colonial hill town: pilotis, clay-tile roof and balconied duplex rooms.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: early Niemeyer, backed by Lúcio Costa

photos.file: File:Grande Hotel de Ouro Preto, vista aérea.jpg

note: Lúcio Costa backed Niemeyer's modern design over a neo-colonial one for this UNESCO town.

name: Brasília TV Tower
features: Steel lattice mast on a concrete base with a viewing deck, set on Brasília's Monumental Axis.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Lúcio Costa's Brasília (UNESCO 1987)

photos.file: File:Brasilia Television Tower from East contre-jour.jpg

note: Fourth photo is an aerial down the axis.

name: Morumbi Stadium (Estádio Cícero Pompeu de Toledo)
features: Huge oval concrete bowl in three tiers, by the leader of São Paulo's brutalist school.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: key work of Vilanova Artigas

photos.file: File:Fachada do Estádio do Morumbi em 2023.jpg
File:Estádio Cícero Pompeu de Toledo (Estádio do Morumbi)João Batista Vilanova Artigas (5877877663).jpg

note: Opened 2 October 1960, finished 1970. First photo is a fine aerial. 'CC BY-SA 3.0 de' is a free licence.

name: Conjunto Nacional
features: A whole block on Avenida Paulista: low shopping podium with a roof garden under a 25-storey slab.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: São Paulo's mixed-use landmark

photos.file: File:Conjunto Nacional em 31 de julho de 2025.jpg
File:Conjunto Nacional em preto e branco.jpg

note: Not Daniel Libeskind: David Libeskind (1928–2014) was a Brazilian architect. Wikipedia's infobox says 1956 but other sources give 1958–1962; check before publishing the year.

name: Edifício Esther
features: São Paulo's first modernist apartment block: shops below, flats and offices above on a free plan.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: early Brazilian modernism
note: Built 1934–38 (Commons/Wikidata). 'First modernist apartment block in São Paulo' is the usual claim in histories; no English Wikipedia article. Listed by CONDEPHAAT and Conpresp.

name: Brazilian Press Association Building (ABI)
features: Office block wrapped in fixed concrete sun-breakers, among the first brise-soleil facades ever built.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: MoMA 'Brazil Builds' (1943) era; IPHAN-listed
commons_category: Category:Edifício-sede da Associação Brasileira de Imprensa

photos.file: File:Edifício-sede da Associação Brasileira de Imprensa 1.jpg
File:Edifício-sede da Associação Brasileira de Imprensa 2.jpg
File:Prédio da Associação Brasileira de Imprensa (ABI) (013RJ004031).jpg

note: Year (competition 1936, finished 1938) is from general histories; no English Wikipedia article found to confirm. Listed by IPHAN in 1984. Third photo is a historic black-and-white view.

name: Palazzo Mondadori
features: Five-storey glass office box hung from a colonnade of concrete arches of varying spans, over a lake.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: key late work of Niemeyer abroad

photos.file: File:Mondadori headquarters by Oscar Niemeyer, Segrate (Milano) 01.jpg
File:Mondadori headquarters by Oscar Niemeyer, Segrate (Milano) 05.jpg
File:Mondadori headquarters by Oscar Niemeyer, Segrate (Milano) 03.jpg

note: Italy has no freedom of panorama and Niemeyer died in 2012, so these photos could be deleted from Commons later; like Villa Savoye, the owner may prefer a drawing cover. Second photo is the low arched side pavilion; third is under the block.

name: Teatro Cultura Artística
features: Concert hall whose curved street front carries Di Cavalcanti's huge glass-mosaic mural.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: key work of Rino Levi
note: A 2008 fire gutted the interior; the mosaic facade survived and the theatre has been rebuilt behind it. Other photos in the category show the rebuilding.

name: Museu das Missões
features: Glass-walled pavilion under a clay-tile roof, built with stones from the Jesuit mission ruins beside it.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Lúcio Costa for SPHAN, at a UNESCO World Heritage site
note: Small museum of Guarani-Jesuit sculpture at São Miguel Arcanjo; an early mix of modern and colonial by Costa.

name: Brasília Bus Station (Rodoviária do Plano Piloto)
features: Multi-level concrete platform at the crossing of Brasília's two axes: buses below, roads over the top.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: heart of Lúcio Costa's Brasília plan (UNESCO 1987)
note: Photos are high views from the TV tower showing the platform deck; no close ground-level exterior checked.

name: Palácio da Justiça (Ministry of Justice), Brasília
features: Glass box behind a row of concrete arches, with water pouring from chutes between them into a pool.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Niemeyer's Esplanada dos Ministérios

photos.file: File:Brasilia DF Brasil - Ministerio da Justiça - panoramio.jpg

note: Avoid 'Brasilia DF Brasil - Palacio da Justiça DF - panoramio.jpg': it shows the Federal District court, a different building.

name: Edifício Niemeyer
features: Curving apartment tower wrapped in continuous horizontal sun-breaker bands, on Praça da Liberdade.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Niemeyer in Belo Horizonte
note: In the first and third photos the tower is one building in a street view; the second is a close-up of the louvres and base. More Flickr close-ups in the category.

name: Conjunto JK (Conjunto Governador Kubitschek)
features: Two huge slab blocks of flats with shops and services, planned as a city within the city.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Niemeyer's Unité-scale housing

photos.file: File:Conjunto Habitacional Governador Juscelino Kubitschek - Belo Horizonte - 20250908134614.jpg
File:Conjunto Habitacional Governador Juscelino Kubitschek - Belo Horizonte - 20130830142555.jpg

note: Begun 1952, finished 1970. Third photo is black and white.

name: Estadio Olímpico Universitario
by: Augusto Pérez Palacios, Raúl Salinas, Jorge Bravo Moro
features: Earth-banked bowl that reads like a crater in the lava field, with Diego Rivera's stone relief on the east side.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Ciudad Universitaria, UNAM (UNESCO 2007)
note: Main stadium of the 1968 Olympics. The UNAM campus is already on the wall as one entry; this is one of its buildings. Second photo is black and white; third is inside.

name: Rectorate Tower, UNAM
by: Mario Pani, Enrique del Moral, Salvador Ortega Flores
features: Slab tower over a long low wing, with Siqueiros' projecting 3-D mural on its south face.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Ciudad Universitaria, UNAM (UNESCO 2007)
commons_category: Category:Torre de Rectoría de la UNAM

photos.file: File:Ciudad Universitaria UNAM - Torre de Rectoría - 1.jpg
File:Ciudad Universitaria UNAM - Torre de Rectoría - 2.jpg

note: Third photo is a close-up of the facade. Which face carries the mural should be checked against a photo before publishing 'south face'.

name: Torre Insignia (Banobras Tower)
features: 25-storey triangular prism at Tlatelolco, its apex crowned by a 47-bell carillon.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Mario Pani's Nonoalco-Tlatelolco

photos.file: File:Vista de la cara sur de la Torre Insignia desde la av. Ricardo Flores Magón 03 (cropped).jpg

note: 127 m; carillon was a gift from Belgium.

name: National Conservatory of Music, Mexico
features: Pani's music school in Polanco, with an open-air theatre and stone-clad wings round its courts.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: early Mario Pani

photos.file: File:Entrada al Conservatorio Nacional de Música de México.jpg

note: Weak: only two usable files. The first (Flickr Commons, 'no known restrictions') shows the open-air theatre and a wing; the second is mostly the entrance gate and parked cars. 1949 is when the school moved in. Features line is from photos, so check before use; consider dropping.

name: Estadio Azteca
features: Concrete bowl ringed by a frame of raking columns, host of the 1970, 1986 and 2026 World Cups.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Pedro Ramírez Vázquez
note: Renovated for the 2026 World Cup; aerial photos show the new roof.

name: Casa O'Gorman 1929 (Cecil O'Gorman House)
features: Mexico's first functionalist house: a glazed studio box on pilotis with an outside spiral stair.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Juan O'Gorman's functionalist manifesto
note: Only one photo, which is black and white. Built for his father, Cecil O'Gorman, in San Ángel; restored and reopened as 'Casa O'Gorman 1929'. The Rivera-Kahlo studios (already on the wall) are next door.

name: Edificio Basurto
features: Streamline apartment tower in Condesa with rounded balconies and a celebrated snail-shell spiral stair.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Mexico City streamline modern

photos.file: File:Edificio Basurto - Colonia Condesa - Ciudad de México - 1.jpg
File:Edificio Basurto - Colonia Condesa - Ciudad de México - 3.jpg
File:Edificio Basurto - Colonia Condesa - Ciudad de México - 5.jpg

note: Photos are upward views from the street; no full-height view checked.

name: Covered Plaza, University City of Caracas
features: Shaded plaza of free-form concrete canopies, with murals and sculpture by Léger, Vasarely, Manaure, Arp and Calder.
award: MoMA 'Latin America in Construction' (2015) and 'Latin American Architecture since 1945' (1955): University City of Caracas (UNESCO 2000)

photos.file: File:Universidad Central de Venezuela Ciudad Universitaria.jpg

note: Heart of Villanueva's 'synthesis of the arts'. Aula Magna and both stadiums are already on the wall. The 1955 and 2015 MoMA shows both featured the campus; check the exact building lists if the owner wants the award line precise.

name: Centro Simón Bolívar (El Silencio Towers)
features: Twin government towers over a long low base, with Avenida Bolívar passing beneath the complex.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: 1950s Caracas, in MoMA's 'Latin American Architecture since 1945' era

photos.file: File:Centro Simon Bolivar 2013 002 vertical fix version.jpg
File:Tito Caula. Torres del Centro Simón Bolívar, ca. 1965.jpg

note: The thumbnail for the 1965 file showed a framed print on a wall, so it may be a photo of a photo; check before use. Several category files show the newer Plaza Caracas buildings, not the towers.

name: Parque Central Complex
features: Megastructure of tall concrete housing slabs and twin office towers, the tallest in Latin America until 2003.
award: MoMA 'Latin America in Construction: Architecture 1955–1980' (2015) era: Caracas megastructure

photos.file: File:El centro de Caracas, las torres de Parque Central.jpg

note: Built 1970–1983 (west tower 1979, east tower 1983). I believe it is in the 2015 MoMA show, but did not confirm against the checklist.

name: Villa Planchart (Quinta El Cerrito)
features: Ponti's 'butterfly' villa on a hill over Caracas, with thin floating roofs and walls treated as sheets.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: European modernism in 1950s Caracas
note: Only one exterior photo: a wide panorama of the front, which will need cropping for the square tile.

name: Museo de Bellas Artes de Caracas (1976 building)
features: Villanueva's last work: stacked concrete galleries beside his own 1938 museum in Los Caobos park.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: key work of Carlos Raúl Villanueva
commons_category: Category:Museo de Bellas Artes de Caracas edificio 2
note: Photos show the entrance front only. Dates (1938 first building, 1966–76 second) are from memory and Commons categories; check before publishing.

name: Edificio Panamericano
features: Long apartment slab raised on V-shaped concrete pilotis, facing the river at Buceo.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Uruguayan modern housing
note: First photo is a close-up of the pilotis; in the second the slab is behind the radio-station pavilion. Year (built 1959–64) from general sources; check.

name: Faculty of Architecture, University of the Republic
features: Architecture school built round a central patio and pool, with stone-clad wings and a long glazed front.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Montevideo's modern university buildings
commons_category: Category:Facultad de Arquitectura, Universidad de la República

photos.file: File:Facultad de Arquitectura (Universidad de la República) - frente.JPG

note: Year 1946 is the usual completion date; check. Vilamajó's Faculty of Engineering, already on the wall, is nearby.

name: Pan American Health Organization Headquarters
features: Curved glass office slab on pilotis beside a round council chamber wrapped in a concrete lattice.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Uruguayan architect's competition-winning design abroad
note: US building, so photos are safe. A file name says the building is currently closed.

name: Estadio Centenario
features: Concrete bowl built for the first World Cup in 1930, with the Art Deco Tower of Homage over the main stand.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: opening work of the period; FIFA Classic Stadium

photos.file: File:Estadio Centenario (Montevideo) Tribuna Olimpica with Torre de los Homenajes.jpg

note: Photos are from inside the bowl and from the air; the outside of the tower shows in the first.

name: Ministry of Public Works Building
features: Art Deco office tower astride Avenida 9 de Julio, its two end faces now carrying steel portraits of Evita.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: 1930s Buenos Aires
note: The Evita portraits (by Alejandro Marmo) were added in 2011. Argentina has no freedom of panorama for artworks; the portraits are a recent artwork, so a deletion request is possible.

name: Torres de Tajamar
by: Luis Prieto Vial with Bresciani, Valdés, Castillo, Huidobro
features: Four tall apartment slabs (towers A–D) set in gardens beside Parque Uruguay in Providencia.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Chilean modern housing (BVCH, see Unidad Vecinal Portales)

photos.file: File:Torres de Tajamar - Torres C y D.jpg

note: Wikidata says built 1962–64; the Commons category says 1967. 'Santiago's first high-rise housing' is a loose claim: soften or check. Four towers (A–D) per file names.

name: Votive Temple of Maipú
features: Huge concrete basilica with a 63 m stepped belfry, built over 30 years beside the ruined 1818 chapel.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Chile's national shrine

photos.file: File:Basílica de Maipú con forma arquitectónica que imita virgen María con capa.JPG

note: Designed 1948, inaugurated 24 October 1974. One Commons file name says the form imitates the Virgin in her cape; Wikipedia doesn't say so, so I left it out.

name: Museo de Arte Moderno de Bogotá (MAMBO)
features: Salmona's brick museum: four floors of angled rooms on a central stair, lit by large windows and skylights.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: key work of Rogelio Salmona
commons_category: Category:Museo de Arte Moderno de Bogotá

photos.file: File:Bogotá exterior Museo de Arte Moderno MAMBO.JPG
File:Museo de Arte Moderno de Bogotá - MAMBO 1.jpg

note: Wikipedia says designed 1985 without a completion date; other sources give 1979 for the first phase. Check the year before publishing.

name: Avianca Building
by: Esguerra, Sáenz, Urdaneta, Samper y Cía., with Ricaurte Prieto Carrizosa
features: 40-storey office tower on Parque Santander, Colombia's tallest building when finished in 1969.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Bogotá's modern skyline (Germán Samper's firm)

photos.file: File:Avianca desde Eje Ambiental con cra 8.JPG

note: 161 m. Survived a 1973 fire that burned floors 14–37.

name: Petroperú Building
features: Dark office tower rising from a stepped, cantilevered concrete base: the state oil company's brutalist HQ.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: MoMA 'Latin America in Construction' era Lima
note: Weak photos: the first is a grey-sky view (1200×1600); the second is at night among other towers. 'EdificioPetroPeru.jpg' is a better daytime view but only 1152 px wide. Features line is from the photos; check before use.

name: Edificio López Serrano
features: Stepped Art Deco apartment tower in Vedado, its setback crown in the manner of New York skyscrapers.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: 1930s Havana

extras.file: File:Floor Plan of Lopez Serrano Building.jpg

note: First photo is a high view from a neighbouring tower.

name: Hotel Habana Libre (former Habana Hilton)
by: Welton Becket & Associates, with Arroyo y Menéndez
features: Hotel slab over a podium whose front carries Amelia Peláez's huge tile mural; the revolution's HQ in 1959.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: 1950s Havana

photos.file: File:Havana Libre Hotel (Former Hilton) seen from Avenue Carlos Manuel Céspedes - panoramio.jpg

note: Opened March 1958. Third photo shows only the top floors and sign.

name: Biblioteca Luis Ángel Arango
by: Esguerra, Sáenz, Urdaneta, Samper y Cía.
features: Stone-clad public library in La Candelaria, with a projecting upper floor screened by slats.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Bogotá modernism (Germán Samper's firm)
commons_category: Category:Exterior of the Biblioteca Luis Ángel Arango
note: First stage 1958, extended in the 1960s and 70s (concert hall). Dates from general sources; check.

name: Girardot Market Hall (Plaza de Mercado de Girardot)
features: Open market hall under a light concrete roof on slender columns, built to stay cool in Girardot's heat.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Leopoldo Rother, Colombian National Monument
note: Weak: photos show the street front cluttered with stalls and taxis; the roof is the point and no photo shows it well. Built 1946–49 per general sources; check year and features before use.

name: Edificio Polar
by: Martín Vegas Pacheco, José Miguel Galia
features: Glass-walled office tower on Plaza Venezuela, an early curtain-wall high-rise in Latin America.
award: MoMA 'Latin American Architecture since 1945' (1955) era Caracas
note: Commons has a 'Torres Polar' category (e.g. 'Torre Polar I.jpg', 'Torre Polar.JPG', both free and large) showing two dark glass towers on Plaza Venezuela, but I couldn't confirm which one is the 1954 Vegas & Galia building and there is no English Wikipedia article. If someone can confirm, it becomes a photo entry. Facts in this entry are from general histories; check before use.

name: Plaza y Fuente del Bebedero, Las Arboledas
features: A long horse trough of still water ending at a tall freestanding white wall, under eucalyptus trees.
award: MoMA 'The Architecture of Luis Barragán' (1976) checklist
note: No usable photo on Commons ('File:Arboledas.jpg' is CC BY-SA 4.0 but tiny). I know the elements (trough, white wall, eucalyptus) but not their dimensions or exactly how the wall sits relative to the trough, so I didn't draw it. A plan or measured drawing would make it drawable.

name: Casa Prieto López
features: Barragán house in the lava garden suburb of Jardines del Pedregal, with walls and patios set into the volcanic rock.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Barragán's Jardines del Pedregal
note: No photo on Commons and I can't establish the massing well enough to draw it. Private house. Facts from memory; check before use.

name: Chapel of San Vicente de Paúl, Coyoacán
by: Félix Candela, Enrique de la Mora
features: Small chapel roofed by thin concrete hyperbolic-paraboloid shells.
award: Latin American modernism 1930–1980: Félix Candela's shell churches
note: No photo on Commons. I'm not sure how many shells it has or how they meet, so I didn't draw it. Facts from memory; check before use.
